s1.method: I looked at the sheet once at native thumbnail size and asked of each tile: what hits the eye first, is it the jewellery, and does the piece look wanted. Tiles where a large, well-lit product is the hero scored highest. Tiles that lead with a body, a prop or a block of text scored lower, even when they had stop power.

X.complianceNotes: Passes the §7 gate and RULINGS. Banned words: none. 'emerald-green cubic zirconia', 'shell pearls' and '18k gold tone' are all allowed listing words, and there is no lone 'emerald', 'gold' or 'pearl'. Stock: 32, which clears the 20 minimum. Price ₹899 matches. Offers: BUY2 10% and BUY3 20% match the live codes, with no free shipping and no compare-at price. 16.8 mm is the listing figure, so no number is invented. The ad is product-only, with no face and no worn scale issue. Primary text is 125 characters, which is inside 120-180, and the offer ends by character 99.
X.notes: Stop power: on a dark monochrome ground, the two cushion stones are the most saturated thing in the frame. The green 'COLOUR' echoes them, so the selective-colour device reads in the type as well as the picture. At 200 px the green squares and the green word land at once. It stops short of 9 because the pair sits upright, centred and uncropped, which reads as a pedestal shot rather than a monument crop. One message: a stranger would say 'this is the piece everyone notices', and the picture proves the headline literally. Product truth: each stud matches the pack and detail refs: 5 clear CZ, 2 gold stars, 2 shell pearls (large and small), mirror-image pair, circlet left open, and the green stone at the upper edge, never centred. The size tag is present. The light is soft rather than raking. Layout: clean order (headline, piece, card). The size-tag box sits only about 35 px above the right stone. The spec line is about 26 px, right at the minimum. In the Story, all text sits between y 270 and 700, but five stacked blocks are tight and the bottom 40% is dead fabric. Copy: 6 words with one device, and the occasion is correctly the second beat. It is a colour/standout benefit rather than the A4 craft truth in listing words. The Meta text is clean but minimal (125 characters, no COD line). Archetype fit: the A4 elements present are the macro, the size tag, the H1 in the calm corner and the Cormorant beat. Missing are the crop, the 10-35 degree tilt and the hard raking light. The selective-colour device is what carries it. Desire: zari brocade and petals in wedding season give it a luxe feel. There is no skin, and the grey petals verge on cold. Purchase cues: ₹899 is legible at 200 px and larger than the product name. The offer states its value, and the ad lands on the product page. The product name is unreadable at 200 px, but the green stones identify the product.

Y.complianceNotes: Same picture, card, offer and Meta text as X, and the same pass. No banned words. Stock 32. ₹899, BUY2 10% and BUY3 20% are verified. 16.8 mm is the listing figure. No face. 'One bold ear' is not a compliance problem, though it carries a product-reading risk (see notes).
Y.notes: Same picture, so product truth, cues and brand match X. A pixel diff confirms the only change in the Feed is the headline and second-beat zone (y 101-346). Stop power: the headline is all cream, so the green hit at the top goes to the thin italic occasion line. At 200 px that line is a weak, low-contrast teal and adds little stop. One message: 'ONE BOLD EAR IS ENOUGH.' sits over a picture of a pair. Read literally, it says wear one earring, the picture does not prove it, and 'ear' for 'earring' needs decoding. Colouring the occasion line makes 'wedding function' compete with the headline as a second idea. Copy: the meaning needs decoding (the rubric's 5-level anchor). It is no listing truth, and the colour treatment promotes the occasion out of its second-beat role. Archetype fit: the type no longer ties to the selective-colour device. In the Story the occasion line is dropped, so the headline carries no green at all, and the Story becomes generic 'dark macro plus line'. Desire: the picture is unchanged. The line is a restraint pitch ('enough') rather than a desire pitch, which is less aspirational for a wedding-season buyer. Layout is equal to X; the one-line Story headline (x 85-995) is a fair width. Copy at 5.5 puts it below the ship rule's floor of 6.

A.why: I would run X. Its headline and colour treatment both do the picture's job: a monochrome scene where only the stones carry colour, headlined 'THE ONLY COLOUR IN THE ROOM' with 'COLOUR' set in the stone's green. The picture proves the line, the split-colour headline adds stop power at 200 px, and the device survives into the Story. Y's 'ONE BOLD EAR IS ENOUGH' sits over a visible pair, reads as 'wear one', and needs decoding. Its green goes to the occasion line, which weakens the hook and lifts the second beat above the headline, and in the Story that green vanishes. Y's copy (5.5) fails the ship rule's floor of 6. X clears every floor, with product truth at 8.5.

X.complianceNotes: PASS. No banned word on the image or in the Meta text. 'Emerald-green cubic zirconia', '18k gold tone' and 'shell pearls' are all allowed listing words; 'emerald' never appears alone, and neither 'pearl' without 'shell' nor 'freshwater' appears. Stock is 32, so 20 or more. ₹899 and the BUY2 10% / BUY3 20% offers match the RULINGS read of 19 Nov 15:25 UTC. I could not re-check them live today (20 Nov), so check them before launch. No compare-at price, no free shipping, no water imagery, no worn frame, no face. 'About 16.8 mm tall' is the listing height, so no number is invented. Honesty nits that do not fail the gate: (1) 'BUY2: 10% off 2 pieces' and '10% off 2' can be read as if the two earrings of one pair count as 2 pieces. BUY2 needs 2 items, and a pair of studs is 1 item, so 'any 2 pieces' or '2 items' would be safer. (2) The image prints BUY3 · 20% off but the Meta text does not mention it. Both offers are verified, so this is a consistency issue only.
X.notes: Product truth: I checked the picture against the pack and detail refs and the 19 Nov lock. Each stud has a cushion emerald-green CZ at the upper edge of the circlet, slightly tilted, and the centre stays open (the post shows through). Each has 5 claw-set clear CZs, two four-point gold stars, one larger shell pearl on the inner side and one small pearl at the bottom. The pair are mirror images, and the order of parts matches the refs stone by stone. The only drift is small: the green stone sits closer to centre-top than in the detail ref, but it never centres in the ring. The 'SHOWN MAGNIFIED · ABOUT 16.8 MM TALL' tag answers the scale question for a macro, so it reads clearly as a small stud and not a hoop. One literal point: the gold also carries colour, so the scene is monochrome except the stones and the gold tone. Stop: at 200 px the two green stones are the most saturated thing in the frame. The single green word COLOUR (a jade, about #19A47E, close to the stone's highlight) echoes them and gives the headline a split-colour surprise. One message: the picture proves the headline. A grey world with green the only colour tells a stranger 'these green studs are the standout at a wedding function' in one sentence. Copy: 6 words built on the selective-colour device, and the occasion sits as the second beat in ivory italic. But it is a figurative styling line, not the A4 craft truth in listing words. There is also a small logic wobble: Indian wedding rooms are full of colour. Meta primary text is 125 characters and the offer ends at character 99, which is fine. Layout: headline, then piece, then card read in order. The size tag box ends about 33 px above the stone and does not touch it. Text share is about 18%. The Story keeps all text between y 270 and 700. The wordmark sits tight on top of the headline in the Story. Archetype: this is a centred pair on a plinth, not a monument crop. The piece is not tilted 10-35 degrees and no edge crops it, so A4's mechanism is only partly there. Size tag and magnification are present, and the headline at least works the selective-colour device. Desire: charcoal silk, a silver zari edge and white petals give a moody wedding mood. There is no skin, and the light is cool. Cues: ₹899 and the offer box are legible at 200 px, and the price is set larger than the name. Weighted total is about 7.7, and every dimension is 6 or more, so it meets the ship thresholds.

Y.complianceNotes: PASS. Picture, card, offer and Meta text are identical to X, so the same checks hold. No banned words. 'Emerald-green cubic zirconia', '18k gold tone' and 'shell pearls' are allowed. Stock is 32. ₹899 and BUY2/BUY3 match the 19 Nov read; re-check them live before launch. No water, no face, and 16.8 mm comes from the listing. Same nits as X: 'BUY2: 10% off 2 pieces' / '10% off 2' can be misread as the two earrings of one pair, and BUY3 is on the image but not in the Meta text. Here the headline makes that misreading more likely. 'ONE BOLD EAR' plus '10% off 2 pieces' invites the reading 'single earrings, buy both ears and get 10% off'.
Y.notes: Same picture, so the fidelity checks are the same as X: 5 clear CZs, two four-point stars, two shell pearls, the green stone at the upper edge, the centre open, a mirrored pair, all matching the refs and the 19 Nov lock, with the 16.8 mm size tag present. The difference is the headline. 'ONE BOLD EAR IS ENOUGH.' sits over a picture of two studs, so the picture does not prove the headline and the line needs decoding. It could mean one statement earring per look with no necklace, or wearing a single stud, or that the studs are sold singly. That muddles what you get, which is a pair, so product truth drops half a point and purchase cues half a point. Copy hits the rubric's 'meaning needs decoding' level (5). The line is not listing-verifiable, has no craft truth, and does not tie to the selective-colour device. The green has moved to the italic 'for the wedding function.', which spends the scene's one accent colour on the occasion (the second beat) instead of the claim. A thin Cormorant italic in jade on charcoal is also noticeably lower in contrast than ivory (about 4:1 against about 13:1) and fades at 200 px. In the Story the headline becomes one wide line (x 85 to 995) with no second beat and no green word, so the Story loses the colour echo entirely. Stop power still rests on the stones, which are the most saturated thing in the frame, but the type adds no surprise. Archetype fit is weaker than X: no monument crop or tilt, no craft truth, and the headline does not use the selective-colour mechanism. Desire comes from the same moody silk, zari and petal scene. The 'enough' framing reads as restraint rather than want. Weighted total is about 7.0. Copy (5) and archetype fit (5.5) are below 6, and message sits at 6, so it fails the ship rule.

B.why: X, clearly. The picture, card and offer are identical, so the headline decides it. In X the headline is something the picture visibly proves: a monochrome scene where the green stones are the only colour, echoed by the one jade word COLOUR. Anyone gets it at 200 px in one sentence, and the occasion stays a quiet ivory second beat. In Y, 'One bold ear is enough' sits over a picture of two studs. It needs decoding and makes it unclear whether you buy a pair or a single. Paired with '10% off 2 pieces' it can mislead on the offer. It also spends the scene's only accent colour on the occasion line, at lower contrast. X meets the ship thresholds (all 6 or more, product truth 8.5). Y fails them (copy 5, archetype fit 5.5). Before running X, I would change '10% off 2 pieces' to 'any 2 pieces' or '2 items', and re-read price and stock live.
